claims.text: Applying a nanostructured ceramic composite coating will improve the mechanical and physical durability of metal-component surfaces in aggressive environments.
The coating can be deposited by a method such as thermal spraying.
Optimizing the deposition process for adhesion and hardness will produce the intended coating performance.
The coated components will maintain improved performance during aggressive chemical exposure.
The coated components will maintain improved performance during mechanical wear.
The coated components will maintain improved performance at temperatures up to approximately 200°C.
Nanostructured grains and possible toughening phases create a dense, mechanically interlocked barrier.
The dense, mechanically interlocked barrier resists wear.
The dense, mechanically interlocked barrier resists corrosion.
The coating forms a chemically inert barrier that mitigates chemical attack.
The coating forms a physically hard barrier that mitigates mechanical wear.
The coating reinforces the substrate surface and thereby reduces the rate of surface degradation.
Coated components will have higher surface hardness than otherwise identical uncoated components.
Coated components will have substantially lower wear rates than otherwise identical uncoated components.
Coated components will have substantially lower corrosion rates than otherwise identical uncoated components.
The coating may not remain effective under extreme thermal shock or impact loads beyond its design limits.
The magnitudes of the hardness, wear-resistance, and corrosion-resistance improvements depend on the ceramic formulation and deposition parameters.
